claims.statement: The CLI uses a two-stage pipeline: parseCommand in src/cli/commands.ts turns argv into a discriminated CliCommand union, and src/cli/cli.tsx dispatches that value to a runner or the interactive Ink app.

The entrypoint handles the integrations and mcp commands directly via runIntegrationsCommand and runMcpCommand, while every other command (link, workspace, auth, ngrok, cron, ingest, visualize, run, error, help) is routed through runStandardCommand.

runStandardCommand conditionally loads the OpenWiki environment, re-resolves the command through resolveStartupCommand, computes the first-run telemetry notice, and then dispatches on command.kind to link, workspace, auth, ngrok, cron, ingest, visualize, a printable error, non-interactive print, or the interactive Ink App.

parseCommand returns a discriminated CliCommand union (kinds integrations, mcp, link, workspace, auth, ngrok, visualize, ingest, cron, help, run, error); malformed invocations are represented as { kind: 'error', exitCode: 1, message } rather than thrown exceptions.
Any argv that matches no recognized subcommand is parsed as a run command by parseRunCommand, and a leading --help/-h yields a help command.
In a run command --init selects the init command and --update selects update (default chat), and specifying both --init and --update together is a parse error.
The -p/--print flag requests non-interactive output and is rejected with an error unless the run has a message, --init, or --update.

The --language/-l flag's locale is canonicalized via resolveLanguage when valid; an unrecognized BCP-47 value is rejected with a parse error (kind:error, exitCode:1) whose message names the offending value and suggests a BCP-47 code such as ko, zh-CN, or pt-BR, so a typo can never quietly produce an English wiki.
The --modelId/--model-id flag (in both space-separated and =value forms) is normalized with normalizeModelId and validated with isValidModelId, producing an error for invalid model IDs.
--debug sets process.env.OPENWIKI_DEBUG at parse time, and --dry-run is a developer-only flag rejected as unknown outside development mode (NODE_ENV=development or OPENWIKI_DEV=1).

Run mode is personal or code, tracked by modeSource (default, positional, or option); it can be set by a leading positional mode word, a first-slot positional mode word even when flags precede it, or the --mode flag.
An explicit --mode that conflicts with an already-selected non-default mode is a parse error via resolveExplicitMode.
When no mode is selected, a run defaults to personal, but init/update runs with default mode source are promoted to code.

Run mode determines runtime location and output: getRunModeCwd maps code to the current repository cwd and personal to the local wiki directory, and getRunModeOutputMode maps code to repository output and personal to local-wiki output.

shouldRunNonInteractively selects the print path for a non-dry-run run when --print is set or when stdin is not a TTY and the run was asked to start, causing the entrypoint to call runPrintCommand instead of rendering the Ink App.

resolveStartupCommand downgrades a run to an error when interactive chat with no message runs without a TTY, and when a non-interactive run is missing the configured provider's credentials, with a narrow skip for a clean update before credentials are needed.

runPrintCommand and the interactive App share run machinery: both wrap the run in withRunTelemetry, run ensureCodeModeRepoSetup (creating the workflow on init) and code-mode connectors in code mode, and then invoke runOpenWikiAgent.
On failure runPrintCommand writes the error message plus auth 'how to fix' guidance (writePrintAuthFix) and error diagnostics (writePrintErrorDiagnostics) to stderr and sets a non-zero exit code.

integrations install and uninstall require a host target validated against the installation registry, while list takes no target and reports each registered host's status for both components (one row per host and component); parseIntegrationsCommand rejects other actions with a registry-derived usage error.

Integration scope defaults to user (home directory) and switches to project when --project is supplied, using an explicit path or defaulting to the current directory; --force is only valid for install, --personal selects the personal component (not valid for list, at most once, and not combinable with --project), and both --force and --project may appear at most once.

runIntegrationsCommand prints changed/unchanged status with the skill directory and MCP config paths, and after an install prints restart-and-confirm next steps whose wording depends on user versus project scope, or a personal-specific message for the personal component.

The mcp command starts a local stdio MCP server, the repository server or, with the personal positional, the personal server; its --host id must be 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens (isValidHostId), defaults to 'unknown', and its producerActor is resolved from the registry when the host is known.

commandLoadsEnvironment loads OpenWiki's private credential environment only for real run, auth, cron, ingest, and ngrok commands; integrations and mcp deliberately never load OpenWiki model credentials and rely on the host's authenticated session.
commandEmitsTelemetry restricts telemetry emission and the one-time first-run disclosure to real init/update runs, so chat, auth, and ingest sessions record nothing.

The auth command supports oauth (default per-provider), configure, tools, and list actions; --force is valid for every action except tools, providers are validated via isAuthProviderId, and unknown options or providers produce action-specific usage errors.

runAuthCommand executes each auth action: list prints the provider list, configure creates connector config, tools lists a provider's MCP tools, and the oauth action runs OAuth, saves credentials, writes config, and conditionally discovers MCP tools.

The ingest command parses a target of one source, one source instance, or all (default all) and accepts --print/-p, --scheduled, --pull-only, and --modelId/--model-id; runIngestCommand streams text to stdout, passes a terminal takeover confirmation unless the run is scheduled, prints a per-source summary, and exits non-zero if any source errored.
The cron command supports list (no target), pause/resume/delete with the literal all target, and pull-only all <on|off>; any other form is a usage error.

runCronCommand reads the onboarding config, applies pause/resume/pull-only/delete via the scheduling module, persists the updated config, and prints results; schedule listing and mutation output are formatted by src/cli/schedule-format.ts including the schedule header, Mac wake-window (launchd power schedule) block, per-connector status, and mutation summary.
The ngrok start command accepts an optional url positional and --port (default 53682, validated to 1024-65535); runNgrokCommand delegates to startNgrokTunnel.

The visualize command serves a live graph/reader from the wiki directory (default openwiki, default port 4321, opens a browser unless --no-open) or exports a static site with --export <dir>, and --export cannot be combined with --port or --no-open.
shouldPrintStartupError decides that a startup parse error is printed non-interactively (rather than shown in the UI) when print is requested, there is no TTY, or a run was explicitly asked to start.
The interactive App handles help and error views and auto-exits when the startup command is a real (non-dry-run, non-print) init or update run via shouldAutoExitStartupRun.

writePrintErrorDiagnostics renders ErrorDiagnostic entries from getErrorDiagnostics; OpenRouter metadata (provider_name, is_byok, finish_reason, raw, previous_errors capped at five) and any openRouterDebug payload are always extracted regardless of debug mode, and the final list is deduped by label:value.

When OPENWIKI_DEBUG is set and the error is an Error instance, getErrorDiagnostics additionally emits the error name, a sanitized message, an httpStatusFromMessage diagnostic (the first 4xx/5xx value found in the message), and a stack diagnostic, and widens the walk to nested cause/error/response objects and other allowlisted fields.

The stack diagnostic is sanitized via sanitizeDiagnosticText (which redacts live secret-bearing environment-variable values and bearer-token / known provider key patterns such as sk-or-v1-…) and truncated to 2,000 characters with a trailing ellipsis so a long trace cannot flood the terminal; in debug mode getErrorDiagnostics additionally walks the cause chain to its innermost error and reports it as rootCause (its sanitized message plus allowlisted fields), so a generic wrapper like "Connection error." is accompanied by the actual cause beneath it rather than the same message repeated at every level.

openwiki link [directory] opens the interactive wiki-workspace manager (runLinkCommand), requires an interactive terminal, resolves a repository finder root from the directory (default .), renders the Ink WikiWorkspaceManager, and on submit saves the workspace collection; more than one argument or a leading-dash argument is a parse error.

openwiki workspace supports use <workspace> (activate by ID/name), current (describe active workspace), and clear (clear active workspace), resolved against the repository root by runWorkspaceCommand; any other form is a parse error.
Neither link nor workspace loads OpenWiki model credentials (commandLoadsEnvironment returns false for both) nor emits telemetry.

createTerminalTakeoverConfirmation asks on the terminal whether to take over an expired personal wiki lock and returns no confirmation when stdin or stderr is not a TTY, so with no one to ask an expired lock is never taken over.
